City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
January 25, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:01 p.m. , on January 25, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on January 20, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley
INVOCATION: Mayor Ury
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Conference with Real Property Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8. Property is an approximate 7.126 acre Site, APN 761-072-01 with a common street address of 26742 Oso Parkway, Mission Viejo, California owned by Mission Viejo Oso Parkway Development, LP, a California limited partnership (also known as "Watermarke" or "Andalucia Apartments"). Housing Authority negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager/Housing Authority Executive Director, Charles Wilson, Director of Community Development, James Williams, Economic Advisor, Celeste Brady, Housing Authority Counsel, William P. Curley III, City Attorney. Owner’s negotiators: Greg Neville of Watermarke and counsel Jeffrey Oderman of Rutan & Tucker. Under negotiation: potential acquisition real property interest, a deed of trust that secures long term affordable housing and the price and terms therefor related to the above-listed property pursuant to an Inclusionary Housing Agreement. Factors affecting price and terms under negotiation: recorded covenants and affordable housing requirements to implement City’s Housing Element of the General Plan relating to housing opportunity Site B. Factors affecting time of payment: conditions to closing, due diligence, and schedule of development and completion of the affordable housing project.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received an update on the real estate price and terms for the subject property but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: speaking as the Director of California Alliance to Protect Property Rights, he stated that this City has no blight in the project area, no crime, and no major occupancy problems therefore it does not qualify for redevelopment. He noted that he is pleased to see that redevelopment agencies will be shut down and he will be monitoring the Council’s votes tonight and reporting them to Sacramento.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: questioned the redevelopment agency attorney’s advice over the years and challenged each one of the Council Members to read the information in front of them.
NEW BUSINESS
Special Counsel Celeste Brady provided a history of the City’s redevelopment agency and background on Assembly Bill X1 26. She further outlined the items of business that are before the City Council this evening.
1.
Inclusionary Housing Agreement Between Mission Viejo Housing Authority and Mission Viejo Oso Parkway Development, LP
Special Counsel Celeste Brady presented the staff report.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that he believes the Council is pushing the window with this project and that there are other opportunities.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: reminded the Council of the money that the redevelopment agency gave to the car agencies and she stated that developers may present one thing but they don’t have to deliver if it’s not in their contract.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt Mission Viejo Housing Authority Resolution 12-01 Approving an Inclusionary Housing Agreement Between the Mission Viejo Housing Authority and Mission Viejo Oso Parkway Development, LP; Authorizing the Executive Director to Carry Out the Inclusionary Housing Agreement; and Making Certain Other Findings In Connection Therewith, and (2) include additional provisions in the contract with Mission Viejo Oso Parkway Development, LP which would require the developer to provide a letter of credit or other adequate security in the amount of $4.8 million for Park Fees so that the City can draw on that money in the event that the State of California or the County of Orange takes the Park Fees at a later date.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
Council Member Schlicht noted, for the record, that she believes the Council is overreaching and she voted no to preserve the assets of the CDA. She stated that that is the Council’s statutory obligation, instead of creating contracts and creating debt. She believes that taking $5.7 from the Community Development Agency and putting it into the Housing Authority could possibly be an unlawful act. Council Member Schlicht stated that the State is looking for money and that this action puts a flag next to Mission Viejo’s name.
RECESS
At the hour of 7:10 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:25 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
2.
Resolution Declining to Assume the Housing Assets and Functions of the Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo and Confirming that the Mission Viejo Housing Authority Will Assume the Housing Assets and Housing Functions Previously Performed by the CDA Pursuant To Health & Safety Code §34176; Housing Authority Resolution Accepting the Housing Assets and Functions of the Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo Pursuant to Health & Safety Code §34176
Special Counsel Celeste Brady presented the staff report.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that she hopes that pass-through agencies are making as much money as the City’s attorneys are. She feels that the City was ill-advised on many projects and she questioned the advice that the Council has received in redevelopment matters.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt Resolution 12-06 Declining To Assume The Housing Assets And Functions Of The Community Development Agency Of The City Of Mission Viejo And Confirming That The Mission Viejo Housing Authority Will Assume The Housing Assets And Housing Functions Previously Performed By The CDA Pursuant To Health & Safety Code Section 34176.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt Mission Viejo Housing Authority Resolution 12-02 Accepting The Housing Assets And Functions Of The Community Development Agency Of The City Of Mission Viejo.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Mayor Ury, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
3.
Amendments to the Enforceable Obligation Payment Schedule (EOPS) and Initial Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (IROPS)
Special Counsel Celeste Brady presented the staff report.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that someone should justify the fees for consultants Celeste Brady and Jim Williams.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: reminded the Council that the City was required, by the State Housing Authority, to provide opportunities for developers to build low income housing and the city has already done that.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt CDA Resolution 12-01 , as amended, Amending the Enforceable Obligation Payment Schedule ("EOPS") Pursuant to Section 34169(g) of the Health & Safety Code and the Initial Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule ("IROPS") Pursuant to Section 34169(h) of the Health & Safety Code; and that the City Council, acting as successor agency, by minute order, accept transmittal of the amended Initial Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule from the CDA.
Amendment to CDA Resolution 12-01: reduce the enforceable obligation for legal services and economic/planning counseling services by 50%.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:35 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, February 6, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of February 06, 2012
